evidence_units.claim: • Revenues for NIKE, Inc..
evidence_units.source_quote: • Revenues for NIKE, Inc.. were $11.3 billion, flat on a reported basis and down 3 percent on a currency-neutral basis.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ NIKE, Inc.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ NIKE, Inc. Brand revenues were $11.0 billion, up 1 percent on a reported basis and down 2 percent on a currency-neutral basis, primarily due to declines in EMEA and Greater China, partially offset by growth in North America.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ Wholesale revenues were $6.5 billion, up 5 percent on a reported basis and up 1 percent on a currency-neutral basis, primarily due to growth in North America.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ Wholesale revenues were $6.5 billion, up 5 percent on a reported basis and up 1 percent on a currency-neutral basis, primarily due to growth in North America.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ NIKE, Inc.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ NIKE, Inc. Direct revenues were $4.5 billion, down 4 percent on a reported basis and down 7 percent on a currency-neutral basis, due to a 9 percent decrease in NIKE, Inc. Brand Digital and a 5 percent decrease in NIKE, Inc.-owned stores.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ Revenues for Converse were $264 million, down 35 percent on a reported basis and down 37 percent on a currency-neutral basis, due to declines across all territories.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ Revenues for Converse were $264 million, down 35 percent on a reported basis and down 37 percent on a currency-neutral basis, due to declines across all territories.

evidence_units.claim: • Gross margin decreased 130 basis points to 40.2 percent, primarily due to higher tariffs in North America.
evidence_units.source_quote: • Gross margin decreased 130 basis points to 40.2 percent, primarily due to higher tariffs in North America.

evidence_units.claim: • Selling and administrative expense increased 2 percent to $4.0 billion.
evidence_units.source_quote: • Selling and administrative expense increased 2 percent to $4.0 billion.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ Demand creation expense was $1.1 billion, flat compared to the prior year, as higher sports marketing expense and unfavorable changes in foreign currency exchange rates were offset by lower brand marketing expense.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ Demand creation expense was $1.1 billion, flat compared to the prior year, as higher sports marketing expense and unfavorable changes in foreign currency exchange rates were offset by lower brand marketing expense.

evidence_units.claim: ◦ Operating overhead expense was $2.9 billion, up 3 percent, due to employee severance costs and unfavorable changes in foreign currency exchange rates, partially offset by lower other administrative costs.
evidence_units.source_quote: ◦ Operating overhead expense was $2.9 billion, up 3 percent, due to employee severance costs and unfavorable changes in foreign currency exchange rates, partially offset by lower other administrative costs.

evidence_units.claim: • The effective tax rate was 20.0 percent compared to 5.9 percent for the same period last year, primarily due to a prior period one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit provided by U.S.
evidence_units.source_quote: • The effective tax rate was 20.0 percent compared to 5.9 percent for the same period last year, primarily due to a prior period one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit provided by U.S. tax regulations related to foreign currency gains and losses.

evidence_units.claim: • Net income was $0.5 billion, down 35 percent, and Diluted earnings per share was $0.35, a decrease of 35 percent.
evidence_units.source_quote: • Net income was $0.5 billion, down 35 percent, and Diluted earnings per share was $0.35, a decrease of 35 percent.
